statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail 5% (low) on the closed-venue floor, Stress 52% (elevated), Confidence 86% (high).
recommendation: Tail remains far below the block threshold, so the mapped state stays EA_ON for NQ futures and NAS100 CFD. The only published danger window is the 22:00-00:00 UTC futures reopening, where the forecast carries a WATCH allowance against an unobserved weekend auction.
headline: Nasdaq-100 unquoted at 29,544.15 with about fourteen hours of the CME weekend halt remaining; the IRGC Hormuz claim has stood unconfirmed for roughly four and a half hours and fresh delayed internals show semiconductor-led rotation rather than alignment, easing Stress to 52% while Tail holds the closed-venue floor
body:
The Nasdaq-100 closed the August payroll session on Friday 4 September at 29,544.15, up 61.85 points or 0.21% from a 29,482.30 previous close, after ranging between 29,440.15 and 29,655.22. Price retraced repeatedly in both directions inside that 215-point range, which is the opposite of the persistent no-retracement structure the Tail score measures. CME equity-index futures have been halted since the Friday 21:00 UTC settle and are scheduled to reopen at 22:00 UTC on 6 September. That reopening hour and the first full hour after it are the two WATCH slots of this forecast.

The geopolitical sequence produced no new verified step during the current hour. The most recent development remains the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps statement carried at about 03:03 UTC, saying its naval force struck an American unmanned surface vessel attempting to enter what it described as a restricted area of the Strait of Hormuz. That claim has now stood roughly four and a half hours with no CENTCOM confirmation or denial and no corroborating report, which eases Stress a further point to 52%. It follows Saturday's exchange, in which US Central Command said it had permanently disabled two Iranian crude tankers and destroyed a third after Iranian ballistic missiles were fired at two US warships, and the IRGC counter-claim of attacks on three tankers and three US-linked vessels.

The shared cross-asset context was collected at 06:32 UTC and is inside its ninety-minute freshness window this hour, so it is used as supporting evidence for the first time since the halt began. It is latest-session, delayed data and is not treated as a live price path. It shows internal conflict rather than alignment: all seven tracked semiconductors closed higher, averaging about 2.9% with Micron up 6.1% and AMD up 4.7%, while only three of eight megacaps were higher, the megacap mean was about -1.2% with Tesla down 5.9%, and both software sectors fell. Delayed futures are similarly non-aligned, with the Nasdaq contract marginally positive against a lower Dow contract, gold down about 1.4% and the volatility contract up about 0.8%. Rotation of that kind is a Stress and conviction input, not a Tail amplifier.

The remaining cross-asset evidence is Friday-dated and calm relative to the conflict. VIX closed at 14.53, the 2-year Treasury yield stood at 4.34% and the 10-year at 4.77% on the latest H.15 observation, and WTI settled near $91.48 with Brent near $96.28 after a weekly crude gain close to 9% driven by Hormuz supply risk. The macro impulse into the halt was hawkish: August nonfarm payrolls rose 162,000 against expectations near 53,000, with unemployment at 4.1% and average hourly earnings up 3.1% year on year. The Federal Reserve blackout ahead of the 15-16 September FOMC began on 5 September, so no Fed speaker can extend that impulse before PPI on 10 September and CPI on 11 September.

Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail is held at the 5% closed-venue floor because the pathological price path it measures cannot exist while the venue is shut, and Stress at 52% carries the unresolved chokepoint conflict, the energy premium and a two-day information gap that must clear through a single weekend auction. Confidence rises a point to 86% because current verified levels, yields, oil, volatility and calendar coverage are held and the delayed cross-asset context is usable again, while no live Nasdaq-100 price path exists in any hour of the halt.

lookbackSummary: The preceding 24 hours run from 07:00 UTC on 5 September to 06:00 UTC on 6 September and lie entirely inside the CME weekend halt. All 24 slots are available from published Claude assessments, every one is scored at the closed-venue Tail floor of 4-5% under a normal mode, and every one maps to EA_ON and green. Stress was flat at 38% from 07:00 UTC through 10:00 UTC, climbed from 39% at 11:00 UTC to 42% by 14:00 UTC as the Saturday US-Iran sequence developed, stepped to 48% at 15:00 UTC once the CENTCOM tanker strikes were verified, rose to 52% by 19:00 UTC and peaked at 57% at 20:00 UTC when the IRGC counter-claim and Iran's threat of more severe attacks were published. It then eased to 53% by 02:00 UTC, lifted to 56% at 03:00 UTC on the newly published IRGC unmanned-vessel claim and eased back to 53% as that claim went unconfirmed. Confidence held in a narrow 85-86% band throughout: the assessment kept current verified levels, yields, oil, volatility and calendar coverage, but no live Nasdaq-100 price path existed in any of the 24 hours.
outlookSummary: Fifteen of the twenty-four published hours fall inside the CME weekend halt, so no observable Nasdaq-100 price path can form in them; the mapped policy state stays EA_ON with Tail on the 5% closed-venue floor through the dormant hours, lifting from 13:00 UTC as a conditional pre-auction gap allowance and peaking at 14% in the last full hour of the halt. The next two slots are different: futures are scheduled to reopen at 22:00 UTC on 6 September, so those hours are the first in which structure can exist. The reopening hour and the first full hour after it each carry a 20% Tail allowance, map to WATCH and yellow, and together form the only published danger window. The last seven slots step back to 17%, 15%, 14%, 13%, 12%, 12% and 11% and to green on the assumption of an orderly auction into the shortened US Labor Day futures session. Stress opens at 52%, holds that level through the quiet Sunday hours, then rebuilds through the afternoon to a 71% peak at the reopen before easing to a 60% floor. Confidence declines from 86% to 71% because every later slot rests on Friday-dated market evidence and on a geopolitical sequence whose latest step is still an unconfirmed IRGC claim.

Two days of unpriced headlines have to clear through a single auction, and that gap widens the plausible opening dispersion.

Two-day information gap must clear through one weekend auction
No observed structure supports this increment; it is a reservation only

forecast.analysis: The pre-auction allowance widens to 7% with Stress at 55%. The step reflects proximity to the reopen rather than new evidence: the venue is still shut and the last verified geopolitical step remains the unconfirmed IRGC claim. A CENTCOM confirmation or denial before the auction would be the first thing to reprice.
drivers: Tail 7% on proximity to the 22:00 UTC reopen, not on observed structure
Checkpoint: any CENTCOM confirmation or denial of the IRGC claim
Stress 55% as unpriced weekend headlines continue to accumulate

forecast.analysis: Halt continues with Tail at 8%. Weekend news liquidity is thinnest in the hours before a Sunday reopen, so a new escalation step published in this window would carry more gap weight than the same story would on a weekday. Nothing of that kind has been observed and the score remains a reservation.
drivers: Thin weekend news liquidity raises the gap weight of any new headline
Tail 8% remains an unobserved pre-auction reservation

forecast.analysis: Six hours to the scheduled reopen with Tail at 9%. Stress rises faster than Tail by construction: the conflict raises the probability of a large repricing, while the no-retracement path Tail measures also needs persistence that a single opening gap does not by itself establish.
drivers: Stress 58% rising faster than Tail 9% by construction
A gap is a level shock; Tail needs persistent failure of retracement
Six hours remain to the scheduled 22:00 UTC reopen

forecast.analysis: Tail reaches double digits at 10%, five hours before the auction. The Monday session behind the reopen is the US Labor Day holiday, so cash equities are shut and futures run a shortened session on thinner liquidity. Thin follow-through can exaggerate a gap and can equally fail to sustain one.
drivers: Monday 7 September is US Labor Day: cash equities closed, futures shortened
Holiday liquidity can exaggerate a gap but also fails to sustain trends
Tail 10% five hours ahead of the scheduled auction

forecast.analysis: Four hours out at Tail 11% and Stress 62%. The two scores separate further because the evidence behind them differs: the conflict and the crude premium are verified and feed Stress, while every input that could justify a higher Tail - shallow pullbacks, failed retracements, extension - stays unobservable until a price exists.
drivers: Verified conflict and crude premium feed Stress; Tail inputs stay unobservable
Shallow pullbacks and failed retracements cannot be scored on a closed venue
Four hours to the reopen, with Tail 11% and Stress 62%

forecast.analysis: Three hours to the auction with Tail at 12%. Asian dealing desks reopen shortly after the futures restart, so the first Nasdaq-100 prints would be set in a session that also has to absorb the weekend Hormuz sequence across energy and currencies. Cross-asset direction there is the first real read on alignment.
drivers: Asian desks reopen alongside futures; energy and FX absorb the same news
First cross-asset alignment read arrives with the reopen, not before
Tail 12% three hours ahead of the auction

forecast.analysis: Two hours out. Stress at 66% is near its pre-auction peak because the widest plausible repricing sits directly ahead, while Tail at 13% stays well below the block threshold: a wide opening range that then trades back inside itself is a Stress event, not the mean-reversion failure Tail is defined on.
drivers: A wide opening range that trades back inside itself is Stress, not Tail
Stress 66% approaching its pre-auction peak two hours out
Tail 13% remains far below the 25% block threshold

forecast.analysis: Final full hour of the halt, with Tail 14% and Stress 69% at their pre-auction peaks. Every score in this slot is a reservation against an unobserved event. The next hour is the first in which any of it can be tested against an actual Nasdaq-100 price.

forecast.analysis: Asian hours with Tail easing to 15%. The decay assumes volatility fades once the gap is absorbed, which is the normal post-auction pattern and allows Tail to fall quickly when price discovery is orderly. Persistent extension instead would hold the score near its reopening level.

Persistent extension would hold Tail near its reopening allowance

forecast.analysis: Mode returns to normal at Tail 14%. With US cash markets closed for Labor Day there is no cash open behind these hours to re-energise a move, so the usual mechanism that converts an overnight gap into a persistent trend is missing from this particular Monday.
drivers: No US cash open on Labor Day to re-energise an overnight move

forecast.analysis: Late Asian hours at Tail 13%. Stress eases to 62% on the assumption that no new escalation step is published overnight; that is an assumption rather than evidence, and a fresh verified Hormuz development in these hours would reverse the easing before it moved the Tail path.
